tra_loi.vat: Flat cap (newsboy/baker-boy style cap) worn by a man seen from behind
tra_loi.dac_diem: Soft grey, rounded cap with a short stiff brim and a panelled crown that sits close to the head. The man also wears a grey waistcoat over a light shirt. He stands in front of a brick building with a timber post and a doorway.
tra_loi.ly_do: The panelled, peaked flat cap with a stitched crown is a late 19th to early 20th century style. Flat woollen caps existed in 16th-century England, but this design did not. In 1667 men wore wide-brimmed hats, caps or coifs. The waistcoat cut also looks later than 1667.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The bricklayer on the scaffold wears a soft, peaked flat cap, a baker-boy or newsboy style. His collarless work shirt and braces-style apron also look 19th-century.
ghi_chu.ly_do: Peaked flat caps like this are 19th-century working-class headgear. In 1667 a London labourer would wear a knit or felt cap, a broad-brimmed hat or a coif.
